messages:
nate.k: Filing this here in case anyone has seen it . We hit a weird edge with streaming uploads + Authenticator retries on Android where a cancelled call sometimes gets replayed and causes duplicate side-effects on the server. Repro notes below.

joanne.c: Oof. Short summary of our stack? okhttp version, http/1.1 vs h2, any connection pool customizations?

nate.k: OkHttp 4.10.0, Retrofit 2.9, default connection pool, HTTP/2 enabled on emulator image. Uploads are large so we implement a RequestBody that reads from FileInputStream (one-shot). We call into the SDK helper which builds an OkHttpClient via the default AndroidSampleClient builder.

vishal.p: Do you use retryOnConnectionFailure(true)? By default it is true which can replay requests on a fresh connection if the previous stream failed. For one-shot bodies that leads to nonsense.

nate.k: Yes default true. We also rely on Authenticator to refresh tokens on 401. Observed timeline: t0 request started, t1 server reads body and returns 401 mid-stream, t2 okhttp Authenticator triggers token refresh and replays request; but in parallel the original stream finishes and server processes payload as well -> double-processing.

emily.s: Two quick mitigations: (1) set retryOnConnectionFailure(false) for clients that do one-shot streaming uploads, (2) make the RequestBody replayable by buffering small uploads or using a File-based body that supports repositioning (RandomAccessFile) if safe.

joanne.c: Another nuance: HTTP/2 multiplexing can hide stream failures. A cancel or stream error doesn't always map to server abort. If server returns 200 after client call cancelled, the client may still think it failed and retry. We should teach the SDK to surface ambiguous outcomes.

nate.k: Agreed. For SDK parity: our Java (server) SDK has a boolean builder flag "allowAutomaticReplayForStreaming" default false for streaming helpers. Android sample lacks that and uses an all-purpose OkHttpClient. I propose we expose two sample clients in android-samples: one "strict" client for uploads (retryOnConnectionFailure=false, keepAlive short) and one "friendly" client for general low-latency calls.

emily.s: Sounds good. Also add a clear note in docs: "If your RequestBody is non-replayable, prefer disabling automatic retries and/or provide a server-side idempotency token." Example: X-Upload-Id header + server dedupe.

vishal.p: Small code snippet suggestion to make body retry-safe for small files: 
```
class BufferedRequestBody(private val file: File) : RequestBody() {
  private val bytes = file.readBytes() // memory warning: use for < 5MB only
  override fun contentType() = MediaType.parse("application/octet-stream")
  override fun contentLength() = bytes.size.toLong()
  override fun writeTo(sink: BufferedSink) {
    sink.write(bytes)
  }
}
```

joanne.c: For large files we shouldn't buffer. Instead: (A) use an upload session with resumable upload ids, or (B) surface an error to the app and require the app to re-upload when safe. The SDK can provide helper utilities for both flows.

nate.k: Action items I can take: (1) add strict UploadClient sample in android-samples with retryOnConnectionFailure=false, (2) add docs section about HTTP/2 and ambiguous cancellations, (3) add an example showing X-Upload-Id header. I'll open a PR.

infra-bot: created issue ANDROID-SDK-789: "streaming uploads: default client can cause duplicate requests on auth retry" assigned to @nate.k

emily.s: Nice. One more suggestion: add a small runtime check in SDK when a RequestBody implementation throws "contentLength unknown" and retryOnConnectionFailure is true, warn in logs recommending disabling automatic retries for that client. That should help circuits notice misconfiguration.

nate.k: Great idea. I'll implement a log warning + sample change in the PR. Thanks all.
